audits.mathematicalReason: Draw radius OB. Since OB = BC, triangle OBC is isosceles, so ∠BOC = ∠BCO = y. Its exterior angle ∠ABO is therefore 2y. Since OA = OB, triangle AOB is isosceles and ∠OAB = 2y. Finally, x = ∠AOD is an exterior angle of triangle AOC, giving x = ∠OAC + ∠ACO = 2y + y = 3y. The assessed isosceles-triangle and exterior-angle scopes fit this argument; circle concepts supply the equal radii.

audits.mathematicalReason: Use a unit square with A=(0,0), B=(1,0), C=(1,1), D=(0,1). Then M=(1/2,0), N=(1,1/2), and the lines AN and CM have equations y=x/2 and y=2x−1. Their intersection is O=(2/3,1/3). Triangle AOC has area (2/3−1/3)/2=1/6, while triangle ACD has area 1/2. Thus AOCD has area 2/3 of the square. Alternatively, AN and CM are medians of triangle ABC, so O is its centroid and [AOC]=[ABC]/3=1/6. Both listed routes validly support the composite-area calculation.

audits.mathematicalReason: Set E=(0,0), A=(−2,0), B=(6,0), and D=(0,−3). Intersecting-chord products give EC=12/3=4. The center lies on the perpendicular bisectors of AB and CD, hence is (2,1/2). The second route is also valid without chord products: writing the center as (2,t), equality of its distances to B and D gives 16+t²=4+(t+3)², hence t=1/2. audits.mathematicalReason: Let AC=a, CB=b, and CD=h. The shaded area is π((a+b)²−a²−b²)/8=πab/4. Since AB is a diameter and D is on its semicircle, triangle ADB is right-angled at D. Its altitude DC gives h²=ab by similar triangles. Alternatively, with outer radius R=(a+b)/2, Pythagoras gives h²=R²−((a−b)/2)²=ab. The comparison circle has radius CD, not diameter CD, so its area is πab and the requested ratio is 1:4. Semicircles are 180° sectors, making the assessed sector-area scope defensible; both geometric routes are valid alternatives.

audits.mathematicalReason: A roll along a straight side turns the equilateral triangle through 120°. At a square corner, the next turn is 90°−60°=30°. Each circuit contains four turns of each kind. After one circuit, P occupies A's original position, A occupies B's, and B occupies P's; three circuits are needed to restore all labels. Across those circuits there are twelve 120° turns and twelve 30° turns. P is the pivot for four of each kind, so it moves during eight of each. Every moving arc has radius 2 inches. Its total path is 8(2·2π/3)+8(2·π/6)=40π/3 inches. Rotation properties and arc length are the appropriate assessed scopes.

audits.mathematicalReason: Let the equal base angles at B and C be β. In triangle BDF, ∠BDF=180°−β−a. The straight-angle decomposition at D includes this angle, the 60° angle FDE, and b, giving b=β+a−60°. At F, the straight-angle decomposition gives ∠EFC=120°−a. Triangle EFC then gives c=60°+a−β. Adding yields b+c=2a. Thus the triangle-angle-sum, isosceles, equilateral, and supplementary-angle scopes all fit the proposed reasoning.
